key_insight: A large serum proteomics study identified 19 circulating proteins linked to ALS survival, with GSN and IGFBP2 adding prognostic value beyond standard clinical factors and serum NfL.
clinical_relevance: These blood-based protein candidates could help stratify ALS patients more accurately and support more personalized prognosis and trial design.
method: Analyzed 741 ALS patients from independent cohorts in Israel and the UK
Used two orthogonal proteomics platforms: mass spectrometry and Olink PEA
Looked for proteins with consistent survival associations across cohorts and platforms
evidence_signal: The signal is strengthened by replication across two independent cohorts and two different proteomic technologies, with 19 proteins showing concordant survival associations.
watch_item: These are prognostic biomarker candidates, so prospective validation and standardization are still needed before routine clinical use.
paper_title: Circulating protein profiling identifies prognostic biomarkers in amyotrophic lateral Sclerosis
